title: A Nobel Prize for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation
gist: ECB economist Laura Gáti explains the 2026 Nobel to Robert Hall and Michael Woodford: Hall's Euler-equation testing method and Woodford's New Keynesian framework gave stabilisation policy its microfounded toolkit, and the prize shows data cannot replace theory.

insights.claim: Keynesian theory lacked a theory of individual consumption behaviour, a gap exposed by the 1970s oil crises when aggregate relationships failed to hold, prompting the search for microeconomic foundations of macro models.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti
insights.so_what: Explains why modern macro models are built from individual optimisation.
insights.locator: A theory of consumption and a methodology

insights.claim: Hall tested the consumer optimality condition directly instead of estimating a consumption function, implying consumption follows a random walk: nothing beyond current consumption should predict future consumption.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti
insights.so_what: Gives a sharp, data-light test of rational-expectations consumption models.
insights.locator: A theory of consumption and a methodology

insights.claim: Hall gave the regression error term a theoretical meaning as unpredictable news, which tells researchers which parts of a theory to change when data reject it.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti
insights.so_what: This interpretation became a cornerstone of how macro models are developed and tested.
insights.locator: A theory of consumption and a methodology

themes.theme: Woodford and the New Keynesian paradigm

insights.claim: Models with perfectly flexible prices imply supply-driven fluctuations that move the trend itself, so they give no explanation of business cycles and no guidance for stabilisation policy.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti
insights.so_what: Price stickiness is what makes demand-driven cycles and policy relevance possible.
insights.locator: A unified framework for macroeconomic stabilisation policy

insights.claim: Combining sticky prices (Calvo, Rotemberg) with microfounded individual behaviour created the New Keynesian paradigm, which Woodford's 2003 book Interest and Prices consolidated as the three-equation model.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti
insights.so_what: This is the benchmark model used by central banks and policy institutions.
insights.locator: A unified framework for macroeconomic stabilisation policy

insights.claim: Woodford showed optimal policy should close the gap to trend and announce a commitment to a target, because that commitment anchors public expectations and aids stabilisation.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti
insights.so_what: Formal basis for forward guidance and inflation targeting; expectations management is a policy tool.
insights.locator: A unified framework for macroeconomic stabilisation policy

insights.claim: The long-run view of growth theory failed to explain the Great Depression, which led Keynes to a demand-side theory of short-run fluctuations and the New Deal as the first stabilisation policy.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti

insights.claim: The business-cycle toolkit from these laureates contributed to a large extent to successful policy responses to the 2008 financial crisis.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti
insights.so_what: The ECB credits macro theory for crisis response quality.

insights.claim: The Nobel committee's choice is a reminder that increasing data availability cannot substitute for macroeconomic theory, which is indispensable as a lens for making sense of data.
insights.speaker: Laura Gáti
insights.so_what: A central-bank signal that theory-driven models will keep priority over purely data-driven approaches.
